source: 4-loop equal-mass banana, asymmetric ISP basis (psq, msq).  First L=4 oracle benchmark per ROADMAP Phase 3 'Loop number L=4' diversity axis.  Family layout: 5 massive propagators (l1..l4 squared minus msq, plus a 'wrapping' propagator (l1+l2+l3+l4-p1)^2 - msq gluing the four loops back to the single external leg) and 9 ISPs spanning the remaining l_i.l_j / l_i.p1 scalar products.

cpp_sampled_status.result: BLOCKED — C++ throws on `ibp::diffeq: master count differs between Masters and Reduce calls` at the root AMFSystem's diffeq construction.  Root cause is an architectural divergence between C++ (two independent Kira invocations: a Masters-mode preheat followed by a Reduce-mode inner reduction, each with its own (rank, dot) bound) and upstream MMA (a single Kira invocation whose `IBPSystem` output is shared by both `BlackBoxDiffeq`'s preheat-master-detection step and the subsequent `AnalyticReduction` calls).  For L=4 banana at `BlackBoxDot=5`, jpreferred=[J[1,1,1,1,1,...]]: the preheat detects 10 masters at dot=5 (max master JDot=5, e.g. J[1,1,1,1,6]); libp_deriv shifts the dot to 6 in the derivative integrals fed to the inner Reduce; the inner Reduce runs Kira at dot=6 and reports an 11-master set (10 preheat masters + the additional J[1,1,1,1,7]).  C++'s strict equality check at `src/ibp/reduce.cpp:338` then aborts.  Upstream MMA's analogous check (`If[masnew=!=masters, Abort]` at `Kira/interface.m` DifferentialEquation) is vacuously true in its single-Kira-call structure, so MMA completes (385s wallclock).  L=3 banana doesn't hit this because its max master JDot (= 4 at J[1,1,1,5]) is strictly less than BlackBoxDot=5, so derivative-shifted dot=5 stays within the preheat bound.  This is the first oracle-bench-exposed architectural divergence post-v1.0; the fix requires unifying `ibp::diffeq` to a single Kira invocation that handles both master detection and target reduction.  Tracked as a new audit divergence (see `docs/AUDIT_MMA_PARITY.md` D7).
